short: Joint distillation losses are a standard idea worth 1.5-2.0 LRS3 points, less than recipe and masking; LRS3 31.5% trails 16.9% from public data; 4 of 6 languages lack external baselines.
position: The paper [@ma2022multilingual] adds one new component, M02: joint losses that predict pretrained audio and visual representations from video. This is a standard variant of cross-modal distillation already used by LiRA, ASR-is-all-you-need and Hearing Lips [@ma2021lira; @afouras2020asr; @zhao2020hearinglips]; the ten-run ablation shows it helps, by 2.0 points on LRS3 at 595 h and 1.5 points at 1,459 h (Tables 5, S26; inference). The headline LRS3 gain rests more on the recipe (M03): tuning and an improved language model give 5.8 points (Table S9) and time masking 2.7 (Table 5), against 2.0 for both new losses together (inference). On LRS3 (M12) the 31.5% WER follows the field's usual supervised design and is 14.6 points behind a [later] system trained on public data only [@liu2023synthvsr] (inference). The six-language state-of-the-art claim has published baselines only for English and Mandarin; the other four languages are compared only with a baseline the authors trained.
